content.title: All 5 Oscar-Nominated Songs at the 2026 Oscars, Ranked
content.text: Image via Netflix Published Feb 18, 2026, 1:23 PM EST Ross Bonaime is the Senior Film Editor at Collider. He is a Virginia-based critic, writer, and editor who has written about all forms of entertainment for Paste Magazine, Brightest Young Things, Flickchart, The Free Lance-Star, and more. Ross graduated from George Mason University with a focus in communications and journalism and a minor in film and video studies. Ross is a Tomatometer-approved critic, a member of the Washington DC Area Film Critics Association, and a member of the Critics Choice Association. He has loved movies ever since he saw Cinderella in the theater as a kid, he can quote 10 Things I Hate About You and Wet Hot American Summer from memory, and is fascinated by all things Georges Méliès and Charlie Chaplin. Sign in to your Collider account The category of Best Original Song at the Oscars is always an odd one. It often includes some of the biggest songs of the year, or songs that you've never heard of from movies you didn't even know existed — there's seemingly no middle ground. This year's nominees certainly run the gamut, as they include everything from a 4-time Grammy nominee that broke an impressive record to a song from a surprising documentary that didn't receive a release until after the nominations were announced. This year, the Best Original Song category gets K-pop, opera, and blues, in what is a fairly impressive lineup considering how questionable these nominees can often be. Let's rank the five nominees for Best Song at the 2026 Oscars, even though we probably already know which one is (deservedly) winning it. Music and Lyric by Diane Warren Image via Greenwich Entertainment In the documentary/desperate plea for an Oscar, Diane Warren: Relentless, Warren shows her extreme frustration at how she’s been nominated for Best Original Song at the Academy Awards so many times and never won. “Dear Me” marks her seventeenth nomination, and what Diane Warren: Relentless fails to show is just how generic and bland her songs over the last decade have become. There was a point when Warren probably should have won this award, but this last decade has mostly proven that the Academy will nominate Warren no matter what, with the hope that she might break her curse. With songs like “Dear Me,” she never will. 4 “Sweet Dreams of Joy” from ‘Viva Verdi!’ Music and Lyric by Nicholas Pike Image via Viva Verdi! LLC 3 “Train Dreams” from ‘Train Dreams’ Music by Nick Cave and Bryce Dessner; Lyric by Nick Cave Image via Netflix If you want an artist who can encompass the entirety of a man’s life into a little over four minutes, complete with its strangeness, beauty, loss, and disappointments, look no further than Nick Cave. In the title track to Clint Bentley’s gorgeous film, Train Dreams, Cave seems to stand in the shoes of Joel Edgerton’s Robert Grainier, as he sings about the crazy dreams he’s been having about a woman in a field of flowers and a screamin’ locomotive train. Cave presents a life as a series of moments and remembrances, from seeing Elvis Presley drive girls insane to an elk with twisted antlers, but with an underlying sadness that can’t be shaken. 2 “I Lied to You” from ‘Sinners’ Music and Lyrics by Raphael Saadiq and Ludwig Goransson Image via Warner Bros. 1 “Golden” from ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Music and Lyric by EJAE, Mark Sonnenblick, Joong Gyu Kwak, Yu Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Jeong Hoon Seo and Teddy Park Image via Netflix But beyond its accolades, “Golden” is just an absolute banger. It’s unbelievably catchy, and one of the few songs in this category that actually presents the idea of the film through its lyrics. It’s uplifting without being treacly (take notes, Diane Warren), and addictive to the point that you almost have to listen to it more than once at a time. It works without the context of the film, but it works even better if you know the journey of Huntrix. If anything, the biggest surprise about this nomination is that KPop Demon Hunters didn’t have more than one song in the nominations (it appears that they only put forward one song, because, let’s be real, it only needs one nomination). “Golden” isn’t just the best song in this category; it was one of the best songs of 2025, and it’s a no-brainer that it’ll win in this category. KPop Demon Hunters Release Date June 20, 2025 Cast Arden Cho, May Hong, Ji-young Yoo, Ahn Hyo-seop, Yunjin Kim, Ken Jeong, Lee Byung-hun, Daniel Dae Kim, Joel Kim Booster, Liza Koshy, Alan Lee, SungWon Cho, Maggie Kang, Nathan Schauf, Audrey Nuna, Kevin Woo, Lea Salonga, Cori Baik, Jennifer Sun Bell, John Eric Bentley, Ranjani Brow, Esther K.
